title: Pilot go-decision timing and chaos scenarios sync
header: Date/Time: 2027-04-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Morgan, Sanjay, Asha (Redwood) — Elena, Tomás, Priya, Leo (NimbusHealth)
summary: Weekly pilot sync to finalize go/no-go timing and rehearse chaos/fallback scenarios. Reviewed canary ramp schedule, telemetry gating, circuit-breaker thresholds, and runbook owners. Action: send security packet, schedule runbook dry-run, and confirm rollback windows.
topics: Chaos test scenarios and rollback triggers
Cutover timing and traffic steering (A/B vs blue-green)
transcript:
00:00 Morgan: okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. uh quick roll call?
00:08 Elena: Elena here, Tomás, Priya and Leo with me.
00:11 Morgan: great. Sanjay?
00:13 Sanjay: here — hi all.
00:16 Morgan: high level agenda — finalize the go decision window, walk through chaos scenarios, and assign runbook owners. we put the deck in the notes, see slide 7 for the ramp table [link: https://redwood.app/links/nimbus-pilot-deck].
00:31 Priya: quick Q, are we still aligned to the april 14 target for pilot traffic shift?
00:36 Morgan: yes april 14 is tentative go, but we need to lock canary gating and the blackout/rollback windows today.
00:42 Tomás: we ran the load tests yesterday; p50 looks fine, p95 spikes at 1.2s for 1k qps. there were a few tokenization tails on longer prompts, could be kv cache warm-up.
00:55 Sanjay: that matches what we saw in lab — cold start for the KV cache at the 2-3 minute mark. we recommend a warmup traffic pre-roll for 10 min at 1rps per instance.
01:07 Leo: security check — we need confirmation on KMS integration and audit log export retention before we go live. SOC2 docs would help for our internal reviewers.
01:18 Morgan: noted, I'll send the SOC2 and KMS integration guide after the call.
01:22 Priya: perfect. on ramp: what's the proposed canary percentages?
01:26 Sanjay: propose staged canary: 1% initial smoke for 30 minutes, then 5% for 1 hour, then 20% for 2 hours, then full ramp to 100% if no gating trip. these are in slide 9.
01:40 Tomás: can we shorten the 5% window to 30 minutes if telemetry looks very clean?
01:44 Sanjay: yes we can, but need explicit gating thresholds. suggested gating: error-rate > 0.5% over 5m, p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline, or quality regression on sample prompt set (auto-eval).
01:58 Elena: what about A/B vs blue-green? we have a feature flag system that supports both, but want minimal routing complexity.
02:05 Morgan: recommendation is canary + traffic steering (A/B) for the model binary change, blue-green only if infra changes (k8s node config). simplifies rollback path.
02:16 Priya: ok that feels doable.
02:19 Tomás: chaos scenarios — can we walk through a few, like GPU OOM, network partition to db, and model hang?
02:26 Sanjay: sure. Scenario 1: GPU OOM on a dedicated node. fallback: router redirects to lower-capacity variant (quantized) for affected customers, circuit breaker trips at 10% token error rate. Scenario 2: KV cache eviction storm — we see latency spike and elevated cost. mitigation: pause batching and serve with smaller batch size, spin up warmup workers. Scenario 3: external metrics ingestion (datadog) outage — need local retention and buffered flush to avoid blind spots.
02:56 Leo: on the OOM plan, who owns immediate mitigation?
02:59 Tomás: SRE takes first action to drain node and redirect; Redwood SE triggers model fallback if drain exceeds 5min. we need clear handoff.
03:12 Morgan: let's assign owners in action items.
03:15 Priya: also want a smoke test checklist pre-cutover.
03:18 Asha: we have a smoke test template (link in notes) that includes auth flows, top-10 prompt set, and golden-trace comparison. recommend smoke + synthetic load at each ramp stage.
03:32 Speaker 6: there's some transcription weirdness — you said "golden-trace"?
03:34 Sanjay: yeah golden trace, our baseline traces for common prompts.
03:38 Morgan: telemetry gating details: we will create a dashboard in Datadog and a prometheus-exported SLO. gating rules will be codified as alerts: critical (block) and warning (notify). critical thresholds: error > 0.5% sustained 5m, p95 > 1.5x baseline sustained 5m, model-quality drift (BLEU/ROUGE style proxy) delta > 3 points on eval suite.
04:05 Tomás: how do we measure model-quality drift automatically?
04:08 Sanjay: we run an eval harness against the canary responses; if automated similarity score drops below threshold, it fires a quality alert. it's not perfect but it flags obvious regressions.
04:18 Elena: SLA concerns — what is the planned window where we accept degraded performance versus immediate rollback?
04:23 Morgan: we have a 30-minute observation window after each ramp increment where we will not broaden unless gates are green; if critical gates trip, we immediately revert to last stable route. rollback SLA target: < 15 minutes to hit fully reverted traffic.
04:38 Priya: the 15 minute target — is that realistic with our routing stack?
04:42 Tomás: yes with feature flags + nginx layer we can roll back quickly, but network caches might take some time. we should note potential stale client caches.
04:53 Morgan: runbook rehearse — propose Friday April 12th for a dry-run during low traffic (2h window). we simulate OOM and KV storm scenarios, verify alarms and handoffs.
05:06 Elena: can we get a post-mortem template?
05:09 Asha: yes we have a lightweight POC postmortem template, will attach.
05:12 Leo: security run — we need to validate SAML SSO and RBAC rules, and ensure audit logs are forwarded to our SIEM.
05:20 Morgan: Redwood has an SSO integration guide and RBAC doc, will share.
05:25 Priya: pricing/ops question — if we use quantized fallback variant during incident, what's the cost delta?
05:31 Sanjay: typically quantized reduces GPU memory and cost by ~30-40% per token; it's a tradeoff in latency and sometimes slight quality drop we measure in eval harness.
05:42 Morgan: noted for the runbook doc we will include cost estimates per fallback route.
05:47 Tomás: about telemetry retention — how long are token-level traces kept?
05:51 Dev (Observability): default 7 days for detailed traces, aggregated metrics 90 days; extended retention is an add-on.
05:59 Priya: ok that aligns with compliance for now.
06:03 Morgan: let's do a quick readout of next steps and owners.
06:07 Morgan: action items first:
06:09 Morgan: Morgan Blake - send SOC2 + KMS integration guide + SSO step-by-step - due 2027-04-08.
06:16 Asha: Asha Raman - attach smoke test template and postmortem template - due 2027-04-09.
06:22 Sanjay: Sanjay Iyer - prepare automated eval script for canary quality gating and push to repo - due 2027-04-11.
06:30 Tomás: Tomás Rivera - confirm rollback runbook with SRE steps and feature-flag playbook - due 2027-04-10.
06:38 Elena: Elena will coordinate org signoff and compile stakeholder contact list - due 2027-04-09.
06:44 Priya: Priya to create acceptance checklist and confirm traffic windows - due 2027-04-09.
06:50 Leo: Leo to validate SIEM ingestion and KMS key access policy - due 2027-04-10.
06:56 Morgan: next steps: schedule dry-run April 12 (2pm-4pm PDT), send security packet, and finalize canary ramp table in shared sheet. we will meet again April 13 for final go decision review.
07:09 Elena: sounds good, thanks everyone.
07:12 Morgan: thanks team, end call.
